claim: NB7-1 neuroblast produces five U motor neurons (U1-U5) in order.
source: Here, we focus on one stem cell, neuroblast NB7-1, and five of its progeny, the U motor neurons, U1-U5 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Each U motor neuron can be uniquely identified by a distinctive combination of transcription factors in embryos.
source: in embryos each U motor neuron can be uniquely identified by a distinctive combination of transcription factors (Figure 1A) (Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: The text states this explicitly and cites Isshiki et al., 2001, and Figure 1A shows the molecular markers.

claim: U1 and U2 motor neurons have contralateral dendrites that cross the midline.
source: We find dendrites of the earliest-born U motor neurons, U1 and U2, are contralateral (i.e., cross the midline) and dendrites of U3-U5 are ipsilateral (i.e., do not cross the midline) (Figure 1C'–G').
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C'-G'.

claim: U3, U4, and U5 motor neurons have ipsilateral dendrites that do not cross the midline.
source: We find dendrites of the earliest-born U motor neurons, U1 and U2, are contralateral (i.e., cross the midline) and dendrites of U3-U5 are ipsilateral (i.e., do not cross the midline) (Figure 1C'–G').
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C'-G'.

claim: U1 and U2 are generated from NB7-1 while Hunchback (Hb) is expressed in NB7-1.
source: Notably, U1 and U2 are generated from NB7-1 while Hb is expressed in NB7-1 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: There is a correlation between Hb expression and U motor neuron dendrite morphology.
source: Therefore these data establish a correlation between Hb expression and U motor neuron dendrite morphology and raise the possibility of a causal link.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the dendrite morphology data.

claim: Every U motor neuron axon projects to a unique dorsal muscle in embryos.
source: We visualize single U motor neuron axons and their muscle targets and find every U motor neuron axon projects to a unique dorsal muscle (Figure 1C''–G'').
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 1C''-G''.

claim: U1 motor neuron axon projects to muscle 9 (M9).
source: The earliest-born U motor neuron, U1 has the longest axon and reaches the distal most muscle, muscle 9 (M9).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U2 motor neuron axon projects to muscle 10.
source: Progressively later-born U motor neurons have progressively shorter axons, reaching progressively less distal muscles, with U2 reaching muscle 10
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U3 motor neuron axon projects to muscle 2.
source: Progressively later-born U motor neurons have progressively shorter axons, reaching progressively less distal muscles, with U2 reaching muscle 10, U3 reaching muscle 2
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U4 motor neuron axon projects to muscle 3.
source: Progressively later-born U motor neurons have progressively shorter axons, reaching progressively less distal muscles, with U2 reaching muscle 10, U3 reaching muscle 2, U4 reaching muscle 3
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U5 motor neuron axon projects to muscle 4.
source: Progressively later-born U motor neurons have progressively shorter axons, reaching progressively less distal muscles, with U2 reaching muscle 10, U3 reaching muscle 2, U4 reaching muscle 3, and U5 reaching muscle 4.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U1 generates the MN9-1b synapse in L3 larvae.
source: Consistent with embryo data, U1 generates a synapse on muscle 9 that has been called MN9-1b (i.e., motor neuron that targets muscle 9 and has a type 1 big synapse)
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U2 generates the MN10-1b synapse in L3 larvae.
source: U2 generates the MN10-1b synapse
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U3 generates the MN2-1b synapse in L3 larvae.
source: U3 generates the MN2-1b synapse
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U4 generates the MN3-1b synapse in L3 larvae.
source: U4 generates the MN3-1b synapse
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: U5 generates the MN4-1b synapse in L3 larvae.
source: U5 generates the MN4-1b synapse (Figure 1H–J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: In wild type, there is a perfect correspondence between axonal target and neuromuscular synapse for U motor neurons.
source: We conclude that in wild type there is a perfect correspondence between axonal target and neuromuscular synapse
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: A majority of dorsal muscles are innervated by neurons from NB7-1.
source: and that a majority of dorsal muscles are innervated by neurons from NB7-1.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hb in NB7-1 generates ectopic Eve-expressing neurons.
source: Here, we use a previously uncharacterized, NB7-1-specific method to prolong Hb expression. NB7-1-specific manipulation is essential when examining circuit wiring because it rules out possible effects of Hb acting in another lineages. Specifically, we use NB7-1-GAL4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B) to drive Hb expression from either one or two copies of UAS-Hb (Kohwi et al., 2013). In both manipulations, we find an average of ten Eve(+) cells (Figure 2A–D',H).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, 86% of Eve(+) cells have U1 molecular identity.
source: In NB7−1>Hb embryos, 86% of Eve(+) cells are U1-like (Figure 2P-Q and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F-G).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in figures.

claim: In nearly one-third of all hemisegments in NB7-1>Hb, all Eve(+) cells have U1 molecular identities.
source: Furthermore, in nearly one-third of all hemisegments all Eve(+) cells have U1 molecular identities (Figure 2Q arrows).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 2Q.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, Eve(+) cells with U1 identities are born at abnormally late times in development.
source: To demonstrate that in NB7−1>Hb Eve(+) cells with U1 identities are born at abnormally late times in development we measure the distance of each cell body from the CNS midline as a proxy for neuronal birth time, and then plot the position of Eve(+) cells along the medio-lateral axis (Figure 2P and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in figures.

claim: Prolonging Hb expression in NB7-1 decouples a neuron's birth time from its temporal identity.
source: Thus, in NB7−1>Hb, a neuron's birth time and its temporal identity are decoupled, which allows us to parse the contribution of Hb versus other birth time related factors in controlling terminal features of U motor neurons.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, there is a near complete loss of later-born NB7-1 Cas(+) neurons.
source: Second, in Control, later-born NB7-1 interneurons express the transcription factor, Castor (Cas), but not Eve, and are located dorsolaterally to U motor neurons (Figure 2E–E',I). In NB7−1>Hb embryos, there is a near complete loss of the later-born NB7-1 Cas(+) neurons (Figure 2E–F',I).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, extra Eve(+) neurons are generated at the time when neurons with later-born molecular identities are normally born.
source: Taken together, we conclude that in NB7−1>Hb, extra Eve(+) neurons are generated at the time when neurons with later-born molecular identities are normally born.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, all ectopic Eve(+) cells are motor neurons.
source: Regardless of genotype and birth time, every labeled Eve(+) neuron sends a neurite out of the CNS (Figure 3A–D). As a second, independent confirmation that ectopic Eve(+) neurons in NB7−1>Hb are motor neurons, we show a vast majority of Eve(+) neurons from NB7-1 co-stain with the pan- motor neuron marker (phosopho-Mad) (Figure 3E–F). We conclude that in NB7−1>Hb, Eve(+) cells are motor neurons.
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, 77% of U motor neurons have contralateral dendrites.
source: We label 79 U motor neurons and find a majority (77%) have contralateral dendrites (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 4.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, most (79%) but not all Hb(+) U motor neurons have contralateral dendrites.
source: We generate a second set of individually labeled neurons (n = 39), this time staining with Hb, and find most (79%), but not all Hb(+) U motor neurons have contralateral dendrites (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 4.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, Hb expression generates both full and partial transformations of dendrite morphology.
source: Because Hb(+) U motor neurons are generated from NB7-1 that expressed Hb, these data show that in NB7−1>Hb, Hb expression generates both full and partial transformations of dendrite morphology.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Embryonic U motor neuron marker gene expression does not accurately predict U motor neuron dendrite morphology in NB7-1>Hb.
source: Furthermore, these data demonstrate that embryonic U motor neuron marker gene expression does not accurately predict U motor neuron dendrite morphology.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb larvae, there are significantly more MN10-1b branches than MN9-1b branches.
source: We find significant increases in MN9-1b, MN10-1b and MN2-1b branch number (Figure 5K). Counter to our prediction, there are significantly more MN10-1b branches than MN9-1b branches (Figure 5B–F,K).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Expressing Hb in post-mitotic U motor neurons does not increase synapse branching.
source: First, we express Hb in post-mitotic U motor neurons and find no increase in synapse branching (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 5J.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb animals, each U motor neuron generates one or two synaptic branches, as in wild type.
source: Second, we confirm that in NB7−1>Hb animals, each U motor neuron generates one or two synaptic branches, as in wild type (Figure 5L–N).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 5L-N.

claim: Hb has profound effects on neuromuscular synapse formation.
source: In summary, our data reveal an unexpectedly large number of MN10-1b branches on muscle 10 (U2 target) and an unexpectedly low number of MN9-1b branches on muscle 9 (U1 target). These data show that Hb has profound effects on neuromuscular synapse formation
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: U motor neuron embryonic molecular identity does not accurately predict neuromuscular partner in NB7-1>Hb.
source: and suggest that U motor neuron embryonic molecular identity does not accurately predict neuromuscular partner.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, neuromuscular synapses have normal abundance and localization of pre-synaptic and post-synaptic markers.
source: There is normal abundance and localization of pre-synaptic markers—for active zones (Brp), stable microtubule loops (Fustch), and synaptic vesicles (Syn)—as well as post-synaptic markers—for post-synaptic density (DLG) and neurotransmitter receptors (GluRIIA) (Figure 6A–G).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, extra branches on dorsal muscles contain functional synapses.
source: In both Control and NB7−1>Hb animals, within a five-minute imaging period, we find at least one post-synaptic response in every 1b synaptic branch on every muscle imaged (Control [n = 6] and NB7−1>Hb [n = 5] Figure 6H–I and Figure 6—figure supplement 1). We conclude in NB7−1>Hb, extra branches on dorsal muscles contain functional synapses.
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hb in a single neuroblast lineage has profound effects on functional circuit wiring.
source: Taken together this demonstrates that prolonged expression of the temporal transcription factor, Hb, in single neuroblast lineage has profound effects on functional circuit wiring.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, there are 13 examples where neurons with U1 identities innervate either muscle 10 or 2.
source: We label 18 single neurons in NB7−1>Hb and find five examples where embryonic identity and axonal trajectory match as in wild type, and 13 examples where neurons with U1 identities innervate either muscle 10 or 2 (Figure 7A–B').
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Driving Hb with NB7-1-GAL4 results in both full and partial transformations in axonal trajectory.
source: This provides direct evidence that driving Hb with NB7-1-GAL4 results in both full and partial transformations in axonal trajectory.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: There is no strong correlation between the birth time of a neuron and its axonal target in NB7-1>Hb.
source: We generate a second set of singly labeled U motor neurons (n = 52) in a NB7−1>Hb genetic background, and score both the cell body distance from midline and axonal targets. These data reveal no strong correlation between the birth time of a neuron and its axonal target (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 7.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, prolonged Hb in NB7-1 is only sufficient to transiently transform U motor neurons into U1 neurons.
source: In NB7−1>Hb, we stain for Hb at L3, and often found two, and rarely three, bona fide Hb(+) U1/U2 motor neurons (Figure 8E,F), even though in late stage embryos, U motor neurons in NB7−1>Hb expressed Hb as well as other markers of U1/U2 embryonic molecular identity (Figure 8C). We conclude that in NB7−1>Hb, prolonged Hb in NB7-1 is only sufficient to transiently transform U motor neurons into U1 neurons.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Increasing Hb expression level in NB7-1 does not increase the number of bona fide U1/U2 motor neurons at late larval stages.
source: We increase Hb expression by raising NB7−1>Hb embryos at higher temperature or increasing transgene copy number, and confirm the efficacy of these manipulations by showing slightly higher average number of Eve(+) neurons at L3 (Figure 8G). However, there is absolutely no change in the number of Hb(+) Eve(+) neurons at L3 (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 8G.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb, neurons with embryonic U1 molecular marker gene expression are a heterogeneous population.
source: Furthermore, these data demonstrate that in NB7−1>Hb, neurons with embryonic U1 molecular marker gene expression are a heterogeneous population.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb at L3, a majority of individually-labeled Hb(-) U motor neurons project to muscle 10.
source: A majority (n = 7) of the individually-labeled U motor neurons in this dataset are Hb(-) and are therefore not bona fide U1/U2 motor neurons. All of these neurons project to 10 (U2 target).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb at L3, the one Hb(+) bona fide U1/U2 motor neuron targets muscle 9.
source: There is one Hb(+) bona fide U1/U2 motor neuron, which targets the 9 (U1 target).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: There is a significant increase in muscle 9 branches in hemisegments with three versus two Hb(+) neurons in NB7-1>Hb at L3.
source: Next, for each hemisegment, we score the number of Hb(+) U motor neurons at L3 and the number of synaptic branches on s 9 and 10. We pool data for all segments with three Hb(+) U motor neurons and pool data for all segments with two Hb(+) U motor neurons, and find a significant increase in 9 branches in hemisegments with three versus two Hb(+) neurons (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Molecular differences in U motor neurons at L3 correlate with neuromuscular targeting in NB7-1>Hb.
source: These data show that molecular differences in U motor neurons at L3 correlate with neuromuscular targeting.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Expressing VP16::Hb in NB7-1 increases the number of Hb(+) neurons to nearly 5 Hb(+) U motor neurons at L3.
source: First, when we express a wild-type Hb protein tethered to the transcriptional activation domain VP16 (NB7−1>VP16::Hb), in NB7-1 we see an increase in the number of Hb(+) neurons, reaching on average nearly 5 Hb(+) U motor neurons (Figure 9B,D,F).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 9.

claim: In NB7-1>VP16::Hb, the total number of Eve(+) neurons does not increase.
source: Note, that unlike NB7−1>Hb, in NB7−1>VP16::Hb the total number of Eve(+) neurons does not increase, consistent with previous publications (Tran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is directly stated and cites Tran et al., 2010.

claim: Precociously expressing Seven-up in NB7-1 reduces the number of Hb(+) U motor neurons to on average one at L3.
source: Second, we precociously express the Hb switching factor, Seven-up in NB7-1 and other neuroblasts, using the strong EN-GAL4 driver (EN>SVP), and we find a reduction in both the total number of U motor neurons and the number of Hb(+) U motor neurons at L3, finding on average just one Hb(+) U motor neuron per hemisegment (Figure 9C,E,F).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 9.

claim: Genetic manipulations in NB7-1 can permanently alter the expression of Hb in U motor neurons.
source: Together these data show that genetic manipulations in NB7-1 can permanently alter the expression of Hb in U motor neurons.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the number of L3 Hb(+) U motor neurons and the number of synaptic branches on muscle 9.
source: We find a strong correlation between the number of L3 Hb(+) U motor neurons and the number of synaptic branches on muscle 9 (Figure 9G–M).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 9.

claim: There is no significant change in the number of synaptic branches onto muscle 10 when altering the number of L3 Hb(+) U motor neurons.
source: In contrast, there is no significant change in the number of synaptic branches onto muscle 10.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: Early manipulation of gene expression in NB7-1 is sufficient to permanently alter the molecular identity of U motor neurons and to predictably re-wire the neuronal circuits to which they contribute.
source: Taken together these data demonstrate early manipulation of gene expression in NB7-1 is sufficient to permanently alter the molecular identity of U motor neurons and to predictably re-wire the neuronal circuits to which they contribute.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Embryonic molecular identity markers do not accurately predict neuronal terminal features in NB7-1>Hb.
source: One of our most surprising findings is that embryonic molecular identity markers do not accurately predict neuronal terminal features.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a key finding.

claim: Hb can generate complete and partial transformations of neuronal terminal features.
source: These data show that Hb can generate complete and partial transformations of neuronal terminal features, and demonstrate that only in certain contexts does Hb act as a master regulator of temporal-specific developmental programs.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Neuromuscular synaptic partner choice and circuit wiring can be established before neuronal birth by early programs of gene expression acting in neuronal stem cells.
source: Furthermore, we show that manipulation of temporal patterning via manipulation of gene expression in the neuroblast is sufficient to re-wire locomotor circuits, indicating that circuit wiring can be established before neuronal birth by early programs of gene expression acting in neuronal stem cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion.

claim: Hb is a potent regulator of neuromuscular wiring decisions.
source: We find that Hb is a potent regulator of neuromuscular wiring decisions.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract and discussion.

claim: Molecular information acts early in neurogenesis as a switch to control motor circuit wiring.
source: These data introduce important refinements to current models, show that molecular information acts early in neurogenesis as a switch to control motor circuit wiring
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: The mammalian homolog of Hb, Ikaros, acts as a temporal transcription factor in both retina and cortex.
source: Notably, the mammalian homolog of Hb, Ikaros, acts as a temporal transcription factor in both retina and cortex (Alsiö et al., 2013; Elliott et al., 2008).
evidence: This is directly stated and cites two papers.

claim: Temporal patterning has been proposed to play a role in circuit assembly.
source: Temporal patterning has been proposed to play a role in circuit assembly (Deguchi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is directly stated and cites Deguchi et al., 2011.

claim: There is an association between neuronal birth time and neuronal circuit membership in many organisms and many brain regions.
source: In support of such a model, there is an association between neuronal birth time and neuronal circuit membership in many organisms and many brain regions (Bhansali et al., 2014; Deguchi et al., 2011; Eerdunfu et al., 2017; Greaney et al., 2017; Jefferis et al., 2001; Kulkarni et al., 2016; McLean et al., 2007; McLean and Fetcho, 2009; Morrow et al., 2008; Osterhout et al., 2014; Petrovic and Hummel, 2008; Pujol-Martí et al., 2012; Tripodi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is directly stated and cites multiple papers.

claim: U motor neurons are a temporal cohort from the NB7-1 lineage.
source: Here, we identify a temporal cohort in the NB7-1 lineage comprised of U motor neurons (Figure 1). U motor neurons are from a single neuronal stem cell, contingously-born, and because they innervate a group of synergistic muscles they share circuit membership.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: Hb regulates the U motor neuron temporal cohort border.
source: Our data show that Hb regulates the U motor neuron temporal cohort border because when Hb expression is prolonged in NB7-1, NB7-1 produces many more functional, dorsally-projecting motor neurons at the time when NB7-1 would normally be making interneurons.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: Prolonged expression of VP16::Hb does not alter the U motor neuron temporal cohort border.
source: Interestingly, prolonged expression of VP16::Hb does not alter the U motor neuron temporal cohort border.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: A general function of temporal transcription factors is to regulate temporal cohort boundaries.
source: Nonetheless, our data argue that rather than specify specific cell fates, a general function of temporal transcription factors is to regulate temporal cohort boundaries.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: In NB7-1>Hb animals, even the latest-born U motor neuron can adopt terminal features characteristic of the earliest-born U motor neuron.
source: Our data show that in NB7−1>Hb animals, even the latest-born U motor neuron can adopt terminal features characteristic of the earliest-born U motor neuron—including CNS exit, dendrite morphology, axonal targeting and functional neuromuscular synaptic partner selection.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: There is no limit on the ability of late-born neurons to adopt early-born features in NB7-1>Hb.
source: Thus, we find no limit on the ability of late-born neurons to adopt early-born features.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.

claim: Manipulation of temporal patterning via manipulation of gene expression in the neuroblast is sufficient to re-wire locomotor circuits.
source: Furthermore, we show that manipulation of temporal patterning via manipulation of gene expression in the neuroblast is sufficient to re-wire locomotor circuits
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the discussion.
